## Critique
- claim-1: The cited passage supports the two family formulas and the definitions of \(a,b\). It does not by itself identify which is Theorem 1.2’s family and which is Remark 4.7’s family, though that distinction is available from accepted task 170.
- claim-2: The transpose formulas and parameter transformation are correct. However, the proof merely asserts \(\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}\) without explicitly defining the interval ideal and proving this equality basiswise. It also declares the transformed bigrassmannian data admissible without checking the required strict inequality \(t'>r'+s'-n\). Thus the requested fully standalone lemma is not yet established as written.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] State
  \[
  J_{r,q;i,j}:=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
  \]
  and prove basiswise that \(\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}\), using
  \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'\). For
  \[
  (r',s',t',n')=(q,n-s,q-s+t,n),
  \]
  verify every admissibility condition, including
  \[
  t'=q-s+t>q-s=r'+s'-n,
  \]
  as well as \(1\le t'\le r',s'\le n\). Then explicitly apply
  \(\bar\omega_{q,r}\) to the theorem family at \((q,r;j,i)\) to obtain the Remark 4.7 family at \((r,q;i,j)\), and use the isomorphism and its inverse to preserve generation and irredundancy.

## Required revisions
- Add the missing basiswise proof for the interval ideals.
- Complete the transformed-parameter admissibility check.
- Cite the accepted theorem/Remark distinction rather than relying only on source-6’s unordered list.
- State that the target becomes established only after these repairs.
